title: Specified homogeneous vector-bundle sheaves and natural cohomology coactions
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $S,B$ affine $F$-group schemes with $i:B\to S$ [def-sc-group-scheme], and $\pi:S\to Q$ a morphism of $F$-schemes. Use rational modules and their maps from [def-sfb-rational-representation-gzero], the coordinate Hopf algebra and character conventions of [def-sfb-rational-highest-weight-data], and canonical pullback of module sections from [def-sfb-associated-character-line-bundle]. A homogeneous vector-bundle system consists of an $\mathcal O_Q$-module $\mathcal L(M)$ for every finite rational $B$-module $M$, together with natural, $\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$-linear coordinates $\Gamma(Z,(\pi g)^*\mathcal L(M))\simeq\Gamma(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\otimes_F M$ for every $F$-scheme $Z$ and $g:Z\to S$. Require $\pi(gi(b))=\pi(g)$ and require the coordinates at $gi(b)$ to be $b^{-1}$ times those at $g$, using the action obtained by evaluation of the given coordinate coaction at $b$. The coordinates commute with arbitrary pullback. A comodule map $f:M\to N$ is assigned a sheaf map whose pullback in coordinates is $1\otimes f$. Specify an algebraic action of $S$ on $Q$ satisfying $s\pi(g)=\pi(sg)$, and an inverse-action linearization $\tau_M:a_-^*\mathcal L(M)\simeq\operatorname{pr}_Q^*\mathcal L(M)$, where $a_-(s,q)=s^{-1}q$, whose pullback at $(s,\pi(g))$ fixes the coordinates between $s^{-1}g$ and $g$. Do not assume existence or local freeness. Zariski cohomology with the displayed structural scalar map is the existing $H^i$ of [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison], with zero in negative degrees [pqf-def-cohomology]. A natural cohomology coaction $c$ is normalized as follows: if $c(v)=\sum_jv_j\otimes a_j$, then $H^i(\tau_M)a_-^*(v)=\sum_j\operatorname{pr}_S^*(a_j)\operatorname{pr}_Q^*(v_j)$ in the cohomology of $\operatorname{pr}_Q^*\mathcal L(M)$. Pullback here is exact abelian-sheaf inverse image on Ext followed by the canonical adjoint coefficient map. Evaluation is the actual appTop ring map, with its scalar compatibility as a named theorem. The identity coordinate map between the canonical Hopf and algGamma scalar encodings is bijective; this named theorem determines its linear inverse. Define regular left translation on the actual regular-function space by Hopf comultiplication, antipode in the first factor, interchange of factors, and this identity scalar comparison; its formula is $f(s^{-1}g)$. All coordinates, pullbacks, casts along equality of base maps, and tensor-extension maps are the canonical constructions, not freely chosen maps.
